match.reason: None of the bank points compares electric, magnetic and gravitational fields or contrasts attractive and repulsive forces with gravity's attraction-only behaviour; each covers a single field's calculation, and none addresses static versus changing fields.

draft.title: Comparing fields
card: Gravity, electric and magnetic fields each exert a force on a suitable object placed in them. Gravity acts on mass, electric fields act on charge, and magnetic fields act on moving charges and on magnets.

Gravity only attracts, as there is no negative mass. Electric forces can attract or repel, depending on the signs of the charges. Magnetic forces can also attract or repel, such as between like and unlike poles.
A static field does not change with time, such as the field around a fixed mass. A changing field varies with time, such as the field near a moving magnet or a changing current.
In a uniform field the strength and direction are the same at every point, so field lines are parallel and evenly spaced. In a non-uniform field they vary, so the lines bend or change spacing.
draft.remember: Gravity only attracts. Electric and magnetic forces can attract or repel. Any field can be static or changing, uniform or not.

a.q: Which statement correctly compares gravitational and electric forces?
opts: Electric forces can repel, but gravity only attracts
Gravity can repel, but electric forces only attract
Both only attract, but they act on different things
Both can attract or repel, depending on the objects
a.why: Electric forces repel when charges have the same sign. Gravity acts on mass, and there is no negative mass, so it only attracts. The option saying both only attract is tempting, but it ignores like charges repelling.
a.clue: Think about two charges with the same sign.

b.q: Two students compare fields. Which statement about field lines is correct?
opts: Parallel, evenly spaced lines show a uniform field
Parallel lines show a field that is changing with time
Lines that bend apart show a field that is uniform
Evenly spaced lines show a field that only attracts
b.why: In a uniform field, strength and direction are the same everywhere, so lines are parallel and evenly spaced. Whether a field changes with time is a different question from whether it is uniform, so parallel lines do not show a changing field.
b.clue: Uniform describes position, not time or attraction.

a.best: Electric forces can repel, but gravity only attracts

b.best: Parallel, evenly spaced lines show a uniform field
